data.title: Franklin Moves Bitcoin DRIP ETFs Toward Nasdaq With Dividend Reinvestment Plan
data.description:
TL;DR: Franklin Templeton has filed exchange registrations for two stock-and-Bitcoin ETFs. Their strategy redirects equity dividends into crypto exposure, with portfolio rules designed to keep Bitcoin a minority allocation.

Franklin Templeton is moving closer to offering investors a way to combine a US stock portfolio with an automatic Bitcoin allocation. The idea uses dividend reinvestment to build crypto exposure, while periodically trimming it back.

An October 22 Form 8-A registers shares of the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF for Nasdaq. The filing is an exchange-registration step; it does not establish that either fund has begun trading.

For investors, the appeal would be operational simplicity. One fund could handle both the equity portfolio and the rules governing its smaller Bitcoin component, avoiding a separate decision each time a dividend arrives.

Dividends Build Exposure, Rebalancing Cuts It Back

The accompanying prospectus filing proposes an October 27 effective date. It gives the equity version the ticker FBEQ and the innovation version FIBT, with annual management fees of 0.09% and 0.19%, respectively.

The VettaFi indexes started with 95% equities and 5% Bitcoin. Their dividend mechanism reinvests regular and special equity dividends into Bitcoin at the following day’s open after the ex-dividend date.

At quarterly rebalancing, a Bitcoin weighting above 5% is reduced to 4.5%. A separate breach above 20% between reviews triggers a reset to 4.5% at the close of the second following business day. That is a corrective rule, not a guarantee the allocation can never temporarily exceed 20%.

The funds can use Bitcoin-linked investment products and derivatives to reproduce the index exposure. A shareholder would own ETF shares, rather than receive coins in a personal wallet.

Economically, this makes the reinvestment decision part of the product. Dividends are still money belonging to the portfolio. Redirecting them into another asset does not create an extra return by itself, and a lower entry cost for that asset does not guarantee a profitable exit.

A Different Role From A Dedicated Bitcoin Fund

Franklin already offers a more concentrated route through its Bitcoin ETF, EZBC. The issuer describes that product as holding Bitcoin and cash, making its value closely dependent on the coin’s market performance.

The proposed DRIP funds would instead leave most of the investment tied to equities. That means stock selection and the behaviour of the chosen benchmark could matter more to the overall return than a modest move in Bitcoin.

The wrapper also changes the practical meaning of custody. Investors trade fund shares through an exchange; they are not managing the keys or selecting each Bitcoin-related instrument themselves.

The next milestone is the funds becoming effective and opening for trading. Until then, the filings describe a planned allocation strategy, with fees and safeguards to examine, rather than a live track record showing how it performs.

data.title: Franklin Templeton Prepares Nasdaq Debut For ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
data.description:
Key points:
  • Franklin Templeton registered two Bitcoin dividend reinvestment ETFs for trading on Nasdaq on Thursday.
  • The filings follow a June proposal and several delays to the funds' launch date.
  • SoSoValue Data shows the company also operates the Franklin Bitcoin ETF (EZBC), which had around $467 million in assets as of Friday. 

Franklin Templeton has registered two exchange-traded funds (ETFs) for trading on Nasdaq (NDAQ) that will reinvest stock dividends into Bitcoin (BTC), moving the long-delayed products closer to launch. Now, the firm has cleared the last regulatory step to launch its new ETF.

The $1.8 trillion asset manager filed a Form 8-A with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Thursday, registering shares of the Franklin U.S. Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and the Franklin U.S. Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF on the Nasdaq Stock Market. According to a prospectus filed on Thursday, the funds’ registration is now set to become effective on Oct. 27, though Franklin Templeton has not announced a trading date.

How The Funds Work

The Equity fund tracks the VettaFi U.S. Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index, which tracks the 500 largest U.S. companies by market value. DRIP stands for dividend reinvestment plan, and the index will begin with 95% in stocks and 5% in Bitcoin. All regular and special dividends from those companies will be reinvested into Bitcoin at the market open the day after the ex-dividend date.

This process will steadily raise the fund's Bitcoin share over time. If Bitcoin's weight goes above 5% at a quarterly rebalance, it will be trimmed to 4.5%. If it passes 20% between rebalances, it will also be cut back to 4.5%. The fund can gain Bitcoin exposure through exchange-traded products (ETPs), including the ones "sponsored by affiliates of the Fund's investment manager," as well as futures and options.

Franklin Templeton first filed the funds in June but pushed back the effective date several times. The new filing also came the same day investors pulled $635.49 million from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

Bitcoin’s price fell more than 1% over 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Not Franklin’s First Bitcoin Fund

This was not Franklin’s first Bitcoin ETF. It already runs the Franklin Bitcoin ETF (EZBC), which held about $467 million in assets as of Friday, according to SoSoValue Data.

Other funds already mix Bitcoin with traditional assets, including the Simplify U.S. Equity PLUS Bitcoin Strategy ETF (SPBC), which pairs U.S. stocks with roughly 10% Bitcoin exposure, and the STKd 100% Bitcoin & 100% Gold ETF (BTGD), which tracks both Bitcoin and gold.

data.title: U.S. Allies Race to Escape SpaceX's Orbit — WSJ
data.description:
By Sune Engel Rasmussen and Daniel Michaels

LONDON — Elon Musk's decision to abruptly impose limits on Ukraine's use of his Starlink communications network — which is critical to the country's efforts to fight off Russia's invasion — is prompting U.S. allies to intensify efforts to come up with their own alternatives.

Europeans are expressing concerns about relying on a system with a built-in kill switch that gives Musk the power to deactivate a vital network without consultation.

"The more you play politics with your products, the more you damage your brand," Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said to Musk in a post on X after Ukraine reported having problems with Starlink, which is a SpaceX system. Warsaw helps pay for Ukraine's usage of the system.

Even politicians from President Trump's party are sounding alarms. Sen. Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, said Friday that the U.S. shouldn't be "so dependent on one system, one person, one company."

The problem for Starlink customers is that there isn't likely to be a competitive alternative in the near term. The only European company able to operate satellites in low-Earth-orbit where SpaceX dominates is OneWeb, a subsidiary of the French group Eutelsat. OneWeb currently operates roughly 650 satellites and plans to grow its fleet to about 1,300 by 2030, following a 1 billion-euro — equivalent to $1.1 billion — contract signed last month with Airbus.

Starlink already has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit.

OneWeb's older technology is also less suited to Ukraine's front line because of bulky, heavy and power-hungry terminals. Switching from Starlink or its military version Starshield to OneWeb would require replacing thousands of terminals because SpaceX uses proprietary technology.

In a sign of urgency, Ukraine and Finland on Thursday announced that as part of a EUR300 million aid package, Kyiv will join a planned satellite-communications network run by Finnish satellite operator Iceye and networking company Nokia. The first satellites, however, are slated for launch only in 2028.

Canadian satellite-communications company Telesat has also pitched a low-Earth-orbit network, Lightspeed, as offering greater sovereignty. It aims to launch the first of 288 planned satellites in December and become operational by early 2028.

The European Union has contracted with Eutelsat and two other companies to build out a sovereign satellite network of 348 satellites known as IRIS(2), at a cost of about $17.5 billion. The first satellites are slated to launch in 2029.

In Europe, Starlink mostly serves broadband for homes, businesses and airline passengers, as well as limited but growing military use.

What Ukraine's military needs most is technology that is difficult to hack or jam and that provides vast amounts of bandwidth, said Tom Withington, associate fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, a British defense think tank.

"There won't be one technology that replaces Starlink," he said. "They need an amalgamation of different technologies. It will need to be built up over time." He predicted that "Ukraine's ability to do that will surprise people."

European and Canadian funding remains small compared with SpaceX's roughly $2 trillion market valuation. Germany, Europe's largest economy, has committed some $40 billion to space-related defense by 2030. French President Emmanuel Macron last year raised France's space defense budget to roughly $11 billion by 2030, a 70% boost.

The German budget includes funding for orbital surveillance, a satellite operations center and a national constellation of more than 100 satellites in orbit. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called satellite networks "an Achilles heel of modern societies."

Germany is also home to the only private company that has sent a rocket into orbit from continental Europe. Aerospace company Isar last month launched a Spectrum rocket carrying five small satellites. SpaceX's Falcon rocket — on which OneWeb, Telesat and others rely for launches — is more than twice Spectrum's size.

Isar launched from the only site in continental Europe outside Russia with the proven ability to send satellites into orbit: Andøya Space in Norway. Sweden also hosts an orbital launch site in Esrange, about 125 miles north of the Arctic Circle, but the first such launch is planned for 2028.

Given the lack of European launch sites, OneWeb has relied on sites in Russia, Kazakhstan and, after the invasion of Ukraine, Europe's main launch facility in French Guiana, on the northern coast of South America. It has also used an Indian launch site and SpaceX rockets in Cape Canaveral and California.

"From a European perspective, we need to secure an independent launch capacity," said Ketil Olsen, chief executive officer and president of Andøya Space. "We have built an invisible infrastructure through critical services in space. The last few days have exposed how vulnerable we are," he said. "If you don't have your own capacity, you can't control the data."

Andøya Space is 90% government owned, and cannot currently launch satellites of the size required by IRIS(2), the EU network. Andøya's single launchpad is reserved for Isar for up to 20 years, and plans to conduct some 30 launches in the next few years, but Olsen said the company plans to build more pads.

Sweden is also among the European nations moving the fastest in space. In 2024, Stockholm contracted with American aerospace company Planet Labs and Finland's Iceye to send a constellation of roughly 10 military intelligence satellites into orbit, the first of which launched from California in May this year, ahead of schedule.

For now, Sweden relies on the U.S. for launches, which makes it beholden to a busy schedule dominated by commercial actors.

"The demand is higher than the capability. So if you and I wanted to launch something into space, we would have to stand in last in the queue," said Rear Adm. Anders Sundeman, the chief of space for the Swedish armed forces.

Sweden's space program is self-funded, independently of the EU's programs, and relying on multiple partners, even if they are American, helps cushion against the whims of "one single actor," Sundeman said. "It's an American actor that makes the satellite, but we own it and control it," he said.

European efforts are hobbled by bureaucracy, which rarely shows the urgency of commercial actors.

"The main obstacle is leadership," said Serge Plattard, associate fellow at the Foundation for Strategic Research, a French think tank.

The EU's satellite navigation system Galileo, created as an alternative to the American GPS and the Russian Glonass systems, was delayed nearly a decade when it entered into service in 2016. Because member states have yet to fully agree on funding and subcontractors, IRIS(2) is also already poised for delays, Plattard said.

"It is really not safe at all to work the way we're working today in Europe. We are way too slow, and we are unable to anticipate what's happening now in space," he said.

Laurent Jaffart, director of resilience, navigation and connectivity at the European Space Agency, said Europe's efforts to achieve sovereignty in space are driven by a long-term vision rather than individual incidents like the slowdown in Ukraine.

"Recent events nevertheless underline, if not reconfirm, the importance of ensuring that Europe has resilient and sovereign capabilities for essential services," he said.

data.title: Assam: Financial Inclusion Drive held in Kamrup, Loans distributed to rural beneficiaries
data.description:
Guwahati, Oct. 24 -- A major grassroots financial inclusion and credit outreach programme was held at the Malaybari Gaon Panchayat Auditorium near Khetri in Assam's Kamrup (Metro) district, focusing on rural financial security, women's empowerment and entrepreneurship.

The initiative was organised under the flagship Financial Inclusion Campaign led by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Reserve Bank of India (RBI), State Bank of India (SBI) and National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).

The campaign aimed to expand access to institutional credit and government-backed financial security schemes among rural households, with particular emphasis on strengthening women's economic self-reliance and promoting rural entrepreneurship, according to release.

The programme focused on increasing coverage under key financial inclusion schemes, including the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY).

Senior officials emphasised that financial inclusion must extend beyond opening bank accounts to enabling households to build financial resilience through savings, insurance coverage and accessible credit.

As part of the initiative, loan sanction letters and credit cheques were distributed among local beneficiaries and Self-Help Groups (SHGs), providing financial support to expand micro-enterprises, strengthen rural livelihoods and promote small businesses.

The event was attended by SBI Deputy General Manager Amit Ranjan, SBI Chief General Manager Atul Rathi, RBI Regional Director Sushmita Phukan, Lead District Manager Manoj Gogoi, NABARD Assistant General Manager Kirti Prabha and Malaybari Gaon Panchayat President Barnali Hazarika Das, among other officials and local representatives.

The outreach programme also highlighted the broader push towards financial inclusion and rural development in Assam since 2016. Initiatives such as Orunodoi, Self-Help Group credit linkage and doorstep financial services have contributed to expanding access to financial assistance and strengthening livelihood opportunities.

The programme underscored the role of institutional credit, financial literacy and women-led enterprises in promoting rural economic development, reducing financial vulnerability and advancing inclusive growth across the state.

data.title: "US objective is no more oil, nuclear issues, its total destruction of Iran": Foreign Affairs Expert Waiel Awwad
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- As crude oil prices surge to USD 117 per barrel and military tensions escalate across West Asia, Foreign Affairs Expert Waiel Awwad has warned that Washington's ultimate objective regarding Iran extends far beyond nuclear negotiations, aiming instead at complete regime change and regional dominance.

Speaking with ANI, Awwad asserted that conflicting rhetoric from the White House, ranging from threats to annihilate Iran to proposals for dialogue, reflects a deeper strategic shift aimed at reshaping the Middle East in tandem with Israel.

" It's a regime change, is the total destruction of Iran, disintegration of Iran, which makes Israel as a dominant force in the region," Awwad told ANI.

He added that the posture is also driven by domestic political pressure, stating, "This has also created some sort of a reassessment of the situation to improve his scoring in the American midterm election."

Addressing Tehran's retaliatory posture and reports of potential threats to cut Gulf undersea internet cables, the foreign affairs expert emphasised that for Tehran, the conflict has escalated into an "existential war."

"For Iran, it has been now an existential war, and for them, threatening that they will cause a global crisis is nothing but to make sure that if the United States goes this time for a war, Iran is prepared fully to defend itself and also to create more hurt to the United States," he noted.

He expressed scepticism regarding Washington's diplomatic willingness, pointing out that while Tehran had submitted proposals following the UN General Assembly, the US response remained non-committal.

"I don't believe that the United States is serious about the diplomatic outcome of this crisis," he remarked.

With crude oil hitting USD 117 per barrel, the highest level since April, Awwad highlighted the growing economic pressures on India's energy security, domestic inflation, and price stability.

Commenting on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India and the visit to the strategic Reliance refinery in Jamnagar, Awwad pointed out that Washington is seeking to manoeuvre Venezuelan oil supplies into the global market to offset potential supply shocks.

"Jamnagar refinery is not merely a giant factory; in fact, it is one of India's strategic assets, where India can produce more diesel to serve the world and make some kind of balance in the international market," he stated.

He cautioned, however, that escalating conflict across maritime choke points like the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb signals a broader geopolitical clash.

"It's a war of corridors and the war of dominance in the oil market," he said.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Reliance Industries' Jamnagar facilities in Gujarat on Wednesday, home to the world's largest single-site refinery. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor expressed his privilege at accompanying Rubio to Reliance's Jamnagar facilities.

In a post on X, Gor highlighted that India's imports of American liquefied petroleum gas had increased from below 10 per cent to 67 per cent over the preceding year, establishing the United States as India's primary LPG supplier.

Furthermore, he drew attention to Reliance's planned investment in constructing a new US oil refinery, characterising the initiative as a significant opportunity to expand American energy production and create jobs.

Earlier in the day, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that Iran maintained full control over the Strait of Hormuz, asserting that security was being maintained for vessels operating in the region in accordance with Iranian regulations.

The claim came as the IRGC Navy alleged that two supertankers carrying a combined cargo of more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil had struck naval mines while attempting to navigate what Tehran described as an unauthorised southern route through the strategic waterway.

Amid the escalating tensions, Iran warned that it would not allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf, challenging Washington's assertions that Iranian military capabilities had been significantly weakened.

As per Iranian state broadcaster Press TV, Chief of the General Staff of Iran's Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said Iranian forces had rendered the US Navy ineffective in the region.

"The US president must only dream of their military and army entering the Persian Gulf again. They will take this wish to their graves," Abdollahi said. "We will under no circumstances and at no time allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf," he added.

Abdollahi also questioned US President Donald Trump's repeated claims that Iran's nuclear facilities had been destroyed, asking why Washington continued to raise concerns about Tehran's nuclear programme if its facilities had already been eliminated.

"If you have destroyed everything, then what is the meaning of repeating this delusion?" Abdollahi said, alleging that such statements were intended to mislead public opinion.

The latest developments underscore the competing claims by Tehran and Washington over military capabilities, maritime security and the future of energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, amid continued uncertainty over the prospects for a diplomatic agreement.

data.title: India's basmati rice yield likely to be 5-10% higher this year: Industry leader
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- India's basmati rice yield is expected to increase by 5 to 10 per cent this year compared to the previous year, supported by favourable rainfall and better crop conditions, according to Rajeev Setia, President, Basmati IREF, and Joint Managing Director, Chaman Lal Setia Exports Ltd.

Speaking to ANI on the sidelines of the Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 in New Delhi, Setia said the monsoon and subsequent rainfall had supported the growth of the basmati crop, resulting in expectations of higher yields.

"The monsoon was reasonable... and thereafter there were good rains. Just look around, greenery we have all around. So in that way the crop grew and the yield in this particular year for basmati rice is higher," he said.

Asked about the expected increase, Setia said, "It will definitely be 5-10%... higher as compared to the preceding year."

The expected improvement in yields is significant for India's basmati rice industry, as higher agricultural productivity could support export availability amid expectations of growing international demand.

Setia also expressed optimism about the long-term demand for Indian basmati rice, pointing to the increasing popularity of Indian food across international markets.

"The requirement of Basmati is likely to grow in the time to come," he told ANI.

He said Indian basmati rice has established a presence across international markets, while his own company exports to 96 countries.

Setia noted that the growing popularity of Indian cuisine among consumers in Europe and the United States is helping expand the market for basmati rice beyond traditional consumers.

He also highlighted India's position in the global basmati rice trade, noting that the crop has geographical indication (GI) recognition and is cultivated in specific geographical regions.

India is one of the world's leading producers and exporters of basmati rice, with the crop playing an important role in the country's agricultural exports. Higher yields could improve supply availability, although actual export performance will also depend on international demand and market conditions.

The Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 is being held from October 23 to 25 in New Delhi, bringing together Indian exporters, international buyers and other stakeholders in the global rice trade.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Dumps $22 Million in Crypto, Warns of More Pain
data.description:
Arthur Hayes has sold about $22.28 million in crypto from Maelstrom’s directional book. Hayes, the family office’s chief investment officer, confirmed the exit on X and plans to sit out the market.

The post is a shift from his tone earlier this month. On October 15, Hayes urged traders to go long Bitcoin and Ethereum and trade an eventual bailout.

What Arthur Hayes Sold, and Why He Says He Left

Lookonchain data shows his biggest sale was 6,400 ETH, worth $15.2 million. Hayes also sold 14 million Ethena (ENA) for $2.76 million and 323,000 Uniswap for $2.24 million.

Smaller sales included 1.89 million Ether.fi (ETHFI) and stakes in Aerodrome Finance , Pendle (PENDLE), and Zama (ZAMA).

Hayes then confirmed the exit in a post, citing macro and geopolitical risks.

Did Hayes Sell at a Profit This Time?

Hayes says he took profits on ETH and ENA. Lookonchain valued his 6,400 ETH at $15.2 million, or about $2,375 per coin, though his cost for those coins is not public.

ENA offers a clearer comparison. In early August, he bought 9.05 million ENA for about $773,000, or roughly $0.085 per token.

data.title: Investors' recent money moves show a preference for lowering risks over boosting rewards
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Investors have been steadily pouring more money into 'quality' companies than 'momentum' stocks

The AI buildout is not the only thing investors cite as they move toward quality, according to Rene Reyna, Invesco's head of equity ETF strategy.

In a sign that investors are feeling anxious about the outlook for the stock market, they have recently shown a clear preference for "quality" shares, which tend to fare best during periods of broad market declines, over the previously highflying momentum stocks.

The S&P 500 is weighted by companies' market value, which means shares of companies with higher market capitalizations have more influence than those with lower market caps. There are various ways to invest along with the index or to try to outperform it by applying factors to hold subsets of the S&P 500.

If you hold shares of the $818 billion State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust SPY, an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500 SPX by holding all of its stocks, you can see how technology stalwarts and rapid growers dominate. The top five holdings of SPY - Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and two common-share classes of Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) - make up 30.6% of the portfolio.

There are various exchange-traded funds that include S&P 500 stocks but have different risk profiles, including the lower-risk $99 billion Invesco Equal Weight S&P 500 Index ETF RSP, in which each component is weighted the same, the even-lower-risk $19 billion Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF SPHQ, and the more aggressive $22 billion Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF SPMO.

Rene Reyna, Invesco's head of equity ETF strategy, told MarketWatch that flows of new money into the quality ETF (SPHQ) have been steady for most of this year, with positive flows every month except for August. That month, $680 million flowed out of SPHQ, while $714 million flowed into the momentum ETF (SPMO). But in September, the action was subdued and in the opposite direction, with $3.4 million flowing into SPHQ and $43 million flowing out of SPMO. (See below for what constitutes quality and momentum.)

What might make the quality approach work, for now

During the first half of 2026, the equal-weighted approach fared well, with RSP returning 12%, while the S&P 500 returned 10.2%. But SPHQ did even better with a first-half return of 20.8%, while SPMO shined with a 36% return.

SPHQ holds the 100 stocks among the S&P 500 that rank highest according to a quality score that combines returns on equity, debt-to-book value and an "accruals ratio" of operating assets to total assets. The index tracked by this fund is rebalanced twice a year. Each stock is weighted by the product of its quality score and its market capitalization.

SPMO holds the 100 stocks of companies in the S&P 500 with the highest "momentum scores." Twice a year, the components of the S&P 500 are ranked by how much their prices have risen over the previous 12 months, then scored to take volatility into account. The portfolio is made up of the 20% of companies in the S&P 500 that score highest, which are then weighted by a combination of the momentum score and market capitalization

Here's the latest year-to-date performance chart for the three ETFs and the full S&P 500:

The Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF has underperformed the S&P 500 so far this year. The Invesco Momentum ETF tends to outperform the full index during bull markets, but it can underperform during down periods for the broad market.

The chart shows that SPMO has experienced quite a bit of volatility this year, with prices coming down significantly since June 30.

Longer term, SPMO has been a stellar performer, with a five-year return of 137%, against 83% for the S&P 500 and 75% for SPHQ.

But according to Reyna, SPHQ is the safer play for investors during periods of souring sentiment. When asked how SPHQ might help investors who are questioning whether or not the trillions of dollars being spent on the build-out of artificial-intelligence infrastructure will eventually be justified through profits, he said that based on meetings with clients, "the challenge appears to be beyond AI."

He said that prior to the latest U.S. consumer-price index report, which showed inflation at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.7%, "we were looking at a low probability for another rate increase" when the Federal Reserve meets next week.

And Reyna said investors were also watching 10-year U.S. Treasury notes BX:TMUBMUSD10Y, which were yielding 5.02% early on Thursday. He said a 6% 10-year yield would represent a "challenge" to investors, who "might want to take a 6% return rather than the risk in the stock market."

When compared with the S&P 500's price movement, SPMO has had 142.48% upside capture over the past year, with 106.4% downside capture, according to Reyna. Meanwhile, SPHQ has had 86.05% upside capture, with only 61.1% downside capture. Basically, you might not make as much with quality relative to momentum when the market is rising, but you also lose a lot less when the market falls.

For investors who wish to stay invested while softening the effect of a possible market correction, the lower-volatility approach has been gaining in popularity.

-Philip van Doorn

data.title: CoinShares BTF Liquidation Sets Cash Payout And Earlier Options Expiry
data.description:
TL;DR: CoinShares’ Bitcoin and Ether ETF has reached cash settlement. An OCC notice confirms the payout and brings later-dated BTF options forward to a November 20 expiry.

The closing chapter for CoinShares’ Bitcoin and Ether ETF now comes with a precise cash amount and a deadline for outstanding options. The details matter because a fund can stop trading before every contract linked to it has expired.

According to an October 22 notice from the Options Clearing Corporation, liquidation proceeds were distributed at $22.16255605 per BTF share. The adjusted deliverable for a standard options contract is $2,216.26 in cash, replacing its former share-based exposure.

The BTF option symbol remains unchanged. That continuity should not be mistaken for continuity in the investment underneath it: the contract now references a defined cash deliverable rather than an operating crypto fund.

November 20 Becomes The Final Date For Later Series

OCC says series previously expiring after November 20, 2026 will expire on that date instead. Contracts with earlier expirations retain those dates. Existing American-style options remain exercisable before expiry, and exercised contracts continue to settle in one business day.

Settlement is based on the difference between the contract’s total strike amount and its cash deliverable. The adjustment ends the delayed-settlement treatment that applied on October 21.

Those mechanics are separate from a directional view on Bitcoin or Ethereum. Once the deliverable has become cash, subsequent coin-price moves do not recreate the ETF exposure that shareholders previously held.

A Futures Fund Reaches The End Of Its Run

CoinShares announced the closure in September, alongside its Altcoins ETF, DIME. October 20 was the final day for share trading and creation or redemption orders, with liquidation planned around October 21.

The manager said remaining holders would receive cash based on net asset value after provision for the fund’s expenses and liabilities. Its board approved the wind-down following the investment adviser’s recommendation.

BTF’s structure is also relevant. The fund’s own product information describes a portfolio built primarily around Bitcoin and Ether futures, with cash and high-quality debt supporting the strategy. It was not a vehicle that simply kept an equivalent number of coins in custody for every share.

Its published figures as of October 20 showed approximately $15.96 million in assets. That is a dated snapshot of this individual product, not evidence of money leaving every fund managed by CoinShares.

For the wider crypto exchange ecosystem, closures are a reminder that investment wrappers carry their own lifecycles. Fund shares, direct coin holdings and derivatives can respond differently to the same corporate event.

The new information here is the completed payout and the revised options timetable. Treating it as a fresh Bitcoin sale announcement would miss what has actually changed: BTF’s remaining obligations are being resolved in cash.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Trump says he may move White House press corps
data.description:
By Jason Lange

US President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday he may move the White House press corps to a different location.

In a social media post, Trump dismissed a report that he planned to remove the White House press room and restore a historic swimming pool on the site, saying he had never "even thought to do such a stupid thing."

But he said he could relocate the press corps from its current position in the White House.

"I may move the Fake News to a less obnoxious location," Trump said in the post.

The New York Times reported on Tuesday that Trump had urged then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt in August to move news conferences out of the White House's James S. Brady Press Briefing Room, although the idea was never implemented.

According to the report, the president told aides he would rather have an indoor therapy pool that was installed at the site during Franklin D. Roosevelt's administration. The Nixon administration replaced the pool with the press briefing room.

Trump has regularly accused US media of unfair reporting about his administration.

Last month, Trump briefly banned journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House grounds and said other outlets could face similar restrictions. Free speech advocates have said the move violated First Amendment protections for a free press.

The White House reinstated their access after an order from a federal judge who deemed the ban likely unconstitutional, although the Trump administration is still contesting the case.

data.title: Parabilis Medicines Presents Updated Phase 1/2 Data for Zolucatetide Demonstrating Compelling Efficacy and Favorable Safety and Tolerability Profile in Patients with Desmoid Tumors
data.description:
Key points:
  • Objective response rate of 72.2% among response-evaluable patients receiving a starting dose of ≥450 mg at 32-week landmark
  • Disease control rate of 100% across all response-evaluable patients receiving a starting dose of ≥450 mg, with no disease progression and no treatment discontinuations due to TRAEs
  • Data informed FDA-aligned dose and regimen selection for upcoming PEDESTAL Phase 3 registrational trial, with initiation planned in the first half of 2027 and topline results anticipated in 2029
  • Company to host investor webcast on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 CEST (12:00 p.m. EDT)

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Parabilis Medicines , a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to creating extraordinary medicines for patients with serious diseases by unlocking historically undruggable targets, today announced updated safety and efficacy data for zolucatetide, the first and only direct inhibitor of the β-catenin:TCF interaction, in patients with desmoid tumors. The data were presented today in an oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026, taking place October 23–27, 2026, in Madrid, Spain.

The updated results, based on a June 22, 2026, data cutoff, include data from both the dose escalation and dose optimization portions of the ongoing Phase 1/2 trial and reinforce the strong efficacy and favorable safety and tolerability profile observed with zolucatetide. Among response-evaluable patients who began treatment at a starting dose of ≥450 mg, zolucatetide demonstrated an objective response rate (ORR) of 72.2% (13/18) in a 32-week landmark analysis. A disease control rate (DCR) of 100% was observed across all 46 response-evaluable patients who received a starting dose of ≥450 mg, with no disease progression.

Data from a three-arm randomized dose optimization trial supported selection of a 450 mg weekly induction regimen administered for four cycles, followed by 300 mg every two weeks for long-term maintenance. Following productive end-of-Phase 2 discussions, Parabilis has reached alignment with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the selected dose and regimen, on the use of a placebo-controlled study design, and on progression-free survival (PFS) as the primary endpoint for registrational development.

Parabilis plans to initiate the randomized, double-blind PEDESTAL Phase 3 trial (Phase 3 Evaluation of DESmoid Tumor Activity with zoLucatetide) in the first half of 2027, with topline results anticipated in 2029.

“Desmoid tumors are chronic and life-altering for patients, often affecting people at a young age, and patients need treatments that can deliver rapid, deep and durable tumor responses with a tolerability profile suited for long-term treatment,” said Mathai Mammen, M.D., Ph.D., Chairman, CEO and President of Parabilis Medicines. “We designed zolucatetide to directly inhibit β-catenin:TCF, a historically undruggable target at the heart of the biology driving these tumors. The depth and consistency of responses we are seeing, together with the favorable safety and tolerability profile observed to date, reinforce our conviction that zolucatetide has the potential to deliver a truly differentiated medicine and meaningfully expand the number of patients who can benefit from treatment. We are very pleased with the clarity of the FDA’s feedback on our registrational development strategy, and with our Phase 3 regimen selected, we are moving with urgency to bring this medicine to patients.”

Updated Phase 1/2 Results

As of the June 22, 2026, data cutoff, 76 patients with desmoid tumors had been enrolled and treated across all dose levels in the dose escalation and dose optimization portions of the trial. Median age was 37 years (range 19–80), and 69.7% of patients were female. The population included both patients who had previously been treated with and failed gamma-secretase inhibitors (GSIs) and patients naive to GSIs.

A total of 48 patients began treatment at a starting induction dose of ≥450 mg, prior to down-dosing for maintenance. Two patients were started at 900 mg, but had an average dose of 400–500 mg over the first four months of treatment. Of these 48 patients, 46 were response-evaluable, and 18 had scans at 32 weeks. Median time on treatment for this cohort was 4.7 months (range 0.5–22.3), reflecting recent enrollment of a substantial portion of the cohort.

Efficacy

  • ORR per RECIST 1.1 was 72.2% (13/18) among all patients evaluable at the 32-week landmark
  • A disease control rate (DCR) of 100% was observed across all 46 response-evaluable patients
  • Responses were observed irrespective of prior gamma-secretase inhibitor (GSI) exposure or CTNNB1 or APC mutation status
  • No evidence of disease progression or resistance

Safety

  • Zolucatetide continued to demonstrate a favorable safety and tolerability profile at the selected doses for Phase 3 registrational development
  • Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were predominantly low-grade; the most commonly reported TRAEs were fatigue, alopecia and nausea
  • No patients discontinued treatment due to TRAEs
  • Not associated with ovarian toxicity or high-grade gastrointestinal or skin toxicities commonly reported with GSIs

Desmoid tumors are locally invasive soft-tissue tumors that arise in connective tissues and can be aggressive and recurrent, often causing chronic pain, limited mobility, disfigurement and organ dysfunction. data.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 Profit Rises 29%; Net Interest Margin Falls To 4.31%
data.description:
Higher interest income and lower provisions drive earnings growth, while FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation weighs on margins despite strong loan and deposit growth

Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 29 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 4,212 crore for the September quarter of FY27, supported by higher interest income and lower provisions. However, its net interest margin (NIM) declined to 4.31 per cent as the bank mobilised foreign currency deposits during the quarter.

The lender’s standalone profit rose from Rs 3,253 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Consolidated net profit increased 26 per cent to Rs 5,645 crore from Rs 4,468 crore a year earlier, according to its results announced on 24 October.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, grew 16 per cent year-on-year to Rs 8,459 crore from Rs 7,311 crore. Sequentially, NII increased 7 per cent from Rs 7,928 crore in the June quarter.

The bank’s NIM, which measures the income earned from interest-bearing assets relative to their cost, fell from 4.54 per cent a year earlier and 4.53 per cent in the preceding quarter. Kotak attributed the moderation largely to the mobilisation of foreign currency non-resident (bank), or FCNR(B), deposits.

The bank raised around Rs 55,344 crore through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter and extended loans of approximately Rs 16,110 crore through its international branches.

Asset Quality Improves

Provisions declined 15 per cent year-on-year to Rs 803 crore from Rs 947 crore, supporting profitability. Annualised credit cost fell to 0.35 per cent from 0.79 per cent in the year-ago quarter.

Asset quality also improved. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declined to 1.04 per cent of advances as of 30 September 2026, compared with 1.39 per cent a year earlier. Net non-performing assets fell to 0.24 per cent from 0.32 per cent.

The bank’s net advances grew 25 per cent year-on-year to Rs 5.77 lakh crore, while total deposits rose 23 per cent to Rs 6.51 lakh crore. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, deposit growth stood at 13 per cent.

The current account and savings account (CASA) ratio declined to 38.2 per cent from 42.3 per cent a year earlier. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, the ratio stood at 41.8 per cent.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $635M Outflow In A Day As BTC Slips Back To September Levels
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin slid back toward $80,000 on Saturday, more than a month after it last broke that level.
  • U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost over $635 million on Thursday, and $137.94 million on Friday, according to SoSoValue data.
  • Galaxy's Alex Thorn said he is "very confident" the industry will swing back toward decentralized crypto.

Bitcoin’s (BTC) price dropped to around $80,000 on Saturday, a level it last traded at in September, as U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds lost over $635 million on Thursday.

The slide came as investors turned sellers on US spot Bitcoin ETFs, with the funds seeing over $635 million in net outflows on Thursday, according to SoSoValue data. This nearly matched the $681 million the funds lost over the entire week ending October 9.

SoSoValue data also showed it was nearly three times last week's $229 million in outflows.

Bitcoin’s price traded around $80,500, down over 1% over 24 hours, at the time of writing. The drop took the price back to a level it last broke last month, when it traded around the $80,000 range on 18th September.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Oil Adds To The Pressure

Bitcoin's slide also came as oil prices climbed higher. Brent crude rose over 3% on Friday to settle at $116.72 a barrel, its highest settlement since April, as high oil prices stoked inflation fears on Wall Street.

Reports that the U.S. and Israel could be preparing fresh strikes on Iran had revived geopolitical worries. Market participants still priced in a 90% chance that the Federal Reserve would hold rates steady of 375-400 basis points at its meeting next week, according to the CME FedWatch tool, while 10% priced a rate hike of 400 to 425 basis points for the upcoming Oct 27 to 28 Federal Reserve meeting.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said that oil does not move Bitcoin directly. https://x.com/cryptoquant_com/status/2113538742119977146?s=20

According to him, the bigger headwind was the tougher economy that expensive oil created. He noted that Bitcoin's momentum had historically cooled when Brent trended strongly above its yearly average.

Thorn Sees ‘Pendulum’ Swinging Back

Speaking on Galaxy's "Galaxy Brains" podcast, Thorn took a longer view. He described crypto as moving between "the suits," the banks and brokerages that embraced blockchain technology but kept Bitcoin at arm's length, and "the cypherpunks," who backed decentralized money.

He explained that the suits had the upper hand right now, but that has also happened before. Around 2015 and 2016, banks championed "blockchain not Bitcoin" and built private networks, but "ultimately none of those really worked." Thorn said the industry had since swung back. "I've seen it happen, you know, four or five times now, this pendulum swing," he said. "And I'm very confident it will happen again."

He urged Bitcoin holders to "not despair," adding that "Bitcoin is here to stay." While "we can't know for certain," Thorn said it looked "pretty certain" that the $58,000 range Bitcoin touched in June marked the bottom of this cycle.

October has historically been Bitcoin's best month. However, Thorn noted that "we haven't had uh back-to-back uh red Octobers since 2011 and 2012."

Bitcoin, the apex cryptocurrency, was down over 8% year-to-date (YTD).
